headline: Daily research brief — Saturday, October 17

items.detail: VIX rose 21% Friday to 19.99, at the 81st percentile of its one-year range. For SPY, QQQ, AAPL, and MSFT, a single day drives more than 30% of 20-day realized variance, so no clean rich-premium call is valid there. Clean reads only: NVDA implied volatility sits above realized, and TSLA pre-event implied volatility is roughly equal to realized. Avoid selling premium into the TSLA (Oct 21) and MSFT (Oct 28) earnings humps.

items.detail: FRED observations dated Oct 15: effective fed funds 3.88%, 2Y 4.77%, 10Y 5.10%. The 2s10s spread is +33 bp, down from +52 bp 60 days ago as the 2Y rose 58 bp against 38 bp for the 10Y. The 10Y is off its Oct 5 peak of 5.31% but remains a headwind for growth multiples. SOFR exceeds fed funds by 1 bp: no funding stress.
items.title: Rates: 10Y 5.10%, curve flattened, funding calm

items.detail: WTI November settled $101.41 Friday, up 10.4% on the week, with March at $93.53 — a backwardated curve pricing disruption now and fading later. Brent December settled $109.86. The IEA sees diesel stocks unlikely to rebuild before the second half of 2027, and record tanker freight is segmenting the market by route. Grains run the other way: post-WASDE glut and record Brazilian crops coming, with corn, soy, and wheat all in contango. Elsewhere quiet: nothing goes ex-dividend in the four-week window, a SPY Oct-23 box nets −$0.80 executable gross with no arbitrage, and the quant lab scored 19 new candidates with none reaching TEST.
items.title: Energy disruption dominates; dividend window empty, parity clean
